div.head: Hn Lond 12
div.ab: Et si quis thelonium uel consuetudinem a ciuibus Londoñ. ceperit, ciues Londoñ. in ciuitate capiant de burgo uel de uilla, ubi thelonium uel consuetudo capta fuit, quantum homo Londoñ. pro theolonio dedit et proinde de dampno ceperit.

Et si quis thelonium vel consuetudinem a civibus Londoniarum ceperit, cives London. [in civitate] capiant de burgo vel de villa, ubi thelonium vel consuetudo capta fuit, quantum homo London. pro theloneo dedit et proinde de dampno receperit.

And if anyone has exacted toll or tax from citizens of London, the citizens of London within the city shall take from the town or village where the toll or tax was exacted a sum equivalent to that which the citizen of London gave as toll and hence sustained as loss.
div.note: Added October 2026 from Robertson pp. 290–291 (text and translation); Liebermann’s text added from Gesetze I p. 525, October 2026 (two independent readings of the page images)
